paragraphs.text: قَالَتْ : سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ يَقُولُ : « الْمَهْدِيُّ مِنْ عِتْرَتِي مِنْ وَلَدِ فَاطِمَةَ » . قَالَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ : وَسَمِعْتُ أَبَا الْمَلِيحِ ، يُثْنِي عَلَى عَلِيِّ بْنِ نُفَيْلٍ وَيَذْكُرُ مِنْهُ صَلَاحًا . (4285) - حَدَّثَنَا سَهْلُ بْنُ تَمَّامِ بْنِ بَزِيعٍ ، حَدَّثَنَا عِمْرَانُ الْقَطَّانُ ، عَنْ قَتَادَةَ ، عَنْ أَبِي نَضْرَةَ ، عَنْ أَبِي سَعِيدٍ الْخُدْرِيِّ ، قَالَ : قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ ﷺ : « الْمَهْدِيُّ مِنِّي أَجْلَى الْجَبْهَةِ ، أَقْنَى الْأَنْفِ ، يَمْلَأُ الْأَرْضَ قِسْطًا وَعَدْلًا كَمَا مُلِئَتْ جَوْرًا وَظُلْمًا ، يَمْلِكُ سَبْعَ سِنِينَ » .
She said, "I heard the Messenger of Allah say, 'The Mahdi is from my descendants, from the children of Fatimah.'"
Abd Allah ibn Jafar said, "I heard Abu al-Malih praise Ali ibn Nufayl and mention his righteousness."

(4285) Sahl ibn Tammam ibn Bazi narrated to us. Imran al-Qattan narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Said al-Khudri, who said, "The Messenger of Allah said, 'The Mahdi is from me. He has a broad forehead and an aquiline nose. He will fill the earth with equity and justice as it has been filled with tyranny and oppression. He will rule for seven years.'"

quotes.caption: Abu Sa'id's report, Ibn al-Munadi, al-Malahim, p. 188

paragraphs.text: الحسن ، عن العلاء بن بشير (1) ، عن أبي الصديق الناجي ، عن أبي سعيد الخدري ، عن النبيّ ﵌ أنّه قال : أبشروا بالمهدي ، رجل من عترتي ، يخرج في اختلاف من الناس وزلازل ، فيملأ الأرض قسطا وعدلا ، كما ملئت جورا وظلما ، ويرضى عنه ساكن السماء ، وساكن الأرض ، ويقسم المال صحاحا (2) . قالوا : وما صحاحا ؟ قالوا : بالسويّة ، ويملأ اللّه قلوب امّة محمّد ﵌ غناء ، ويسعهم عدله ، حتّى أنّه ليأمر مناديه فينادي : من له إلى مال حاجة ؟ فما يأتيه أحد ، إلّا رجل واحد ، يأتيه فيسأله ، فيقول له : انطلق إلى السادن ، حتّى يعطيك . قال : فيأتيه فيقول له : أنا رسول المهديّ ، لتعطيني مالا ، فيقول له : احث (3) ، فيحثي فلا يستطيع أن يحمله ، فيلقي حتّى يكون قدر ما يستطيع حمله ، فيخرج به ، فيندم . فيقول : إذا ، كنت أجشع امّة محمّد نفسا ، دعتني إلى هذا المال ، وقد تركه غيري ، قال : فيرجع ، فيردّه عليه ، فيقول له : هذا المال لا نقبل منه شيئا ، اعطيناكه . قال : فيلبث بذلك سبعا ، [ أو ] ثمانيا ، [ أو ] تسع سنين (4) ، كذلك لا خير في الحياة بعده (5) .

Al-Hasan, from al-Ala ibn Bashir (1), from Abu al-Siddiq al-Naji, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said, "Receive glad tidings of the Mahdi, a man from my progeny. He will emerge amid disagreement among people and earthquakes. He will fill the earth with equity and justice as it has been filled with injustice and oppression. The inhabitant of heaven and the inhabitant of earth will be pleased with him, and he will distribute wealth in full portions (2)."

They said, "What does 'in full portions' mean?" He said, "Equally." God will fill the hearts of Muhammad's community with sufficiency, and his justice will encompass them, so much so that he will order his caller to proclaim, "Who has need of wealth?" No one will come to him except one man. He will come and ask him, and he will say to him, "Go to the keeper, so that he may give you."

He said, "He will go to him and say, 'I am the Mahdi's messenger, so give me wealth.' He will say to him, 'Take a handful' (3). He will take a handful, but will not be able to carry it. So he will put back enough that he can carry, then leave with it and regret it. He will say, 'Then I am the most covetous soul in Muhammad's community. This wealth called me, while others left it.' He will return and give it back to him, but he will say, 'We do not accept anything back from this wealth. We gave it to you.'"
He will remain thus for seven, or eight, or nine years (4). There is no good in life after him (5).

quotes.caption: Abu Hurayra's report, Ahadith al-Mahdi min Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, p. 64, report 97, citing Musnad Ahmad, vol. 2, p. 336

paragraphs.text: (97) حدثنا عبد اللّه ، حدثني أبي ، ثنا عثمان بن عمر ، ثنا ابن أبي ذئب ، عن الزهري ، عن نافع - مولى أبي قتادة - ، عن أبي هريرة : ان النبي ﵆ قال : كيف بكم إذا نزل فيكم عيسى بن مريم وامامكم منكم . 2 / 336

(97) Abdullah narrated to us. My father narrated to me. Uthman ibn Umar narrated to us. Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Nafi', the freedman of Abu Qatada, from Abu Hurayra, that the Prophet said, "How will you be when Jesus son of Mary descends among you and your imam is from among you?"
Volume 2, page 336.

quotes.caption: Ibn Abbas's report, Bihar al-Anwar, vol. 51, p. 73, from Kamal al-Din

paragraphs.text: 12 - إكمال الدين : ابن مسرور ، عن ابن عامر ، عن المعلى ، عن جعفر بن سليمان ، عن عبد الله بن الحكم ، عن أبيه ، عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس قال : قال رسول الله ﵌ : إن خلفائي وأوصيائي وحجج الله على الخلق بعدي اثنا عشر أولهم أخي وآخرهم ولدي وقيل : يا رسول الله ﵌ ومن أخوك ؟ قال : علي بن أبي طالب قيل فمن ولدك ؟ قال : المهدي يملاها قسطا وعدلا كما ملئت جورا وظلما والذي بعثني بالحق نبيا لو لم يبق من الدنيا إلا يوم واحد لأطال الله ذلك اليوم حتى يخرج فيه ولدي المهدي فينزل روح الله عيسى بن مريم ﵇ فيصلي خلفه وتشرق الأرض بنور ربها ويبلغ سلطانه المشرق والمغرب .

Kamal al-Din. Ibn Masrur, from Ibn Amir, from al-Mualla, from Jafar ibn Sulayman, from Abd Allah ibn al-Hakam, from his father, from Said ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said, "The Messenger of Allah said, 'My successors, my trustees, and Allah's proofs over creation after me are twelve. The first of them is my brother and the last of them is my son.'"

It was said, "Messenger of Allah, who is your brother?" He said, "Ali ibn Abi Talib." It was said, "Then who is your son?" He said, "The Mahdi. He will fill it with equity and justice as it has been filled with tyranny and oppression. By Him who sent me with the truth as a prophet, if only one day remained of the world, Allah would lengthen that day until my son, the Mahdi, emerges in it. Then Jesus son of Mary, the Spirit of Allah, will descend and pray behind him. The earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and his authority will reach the east and the west."

quotes.caption: Imam al-Rida, Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, vol. 2, p. 218

paragraphs.text: قال ﵇ : إذا خرج المهدي من ولدي نزل عيسى بن مريم ﵇ فصلى خلفه
He said, “When the Mahdi from among my descendants emerges, Jesus son of Mary will descend and pray behind him.”

quotes.caption: Gabriel's words to the Prophet, al-Kafi, vol. 8, p. 74, hadith 10

paragraphs.text: ومنكم القائم يصلي عيسى بن مريم خلفه إذا أهبطه الله إلى الأرض من ذرية علي وفاطمة من ولد الحسين (﵈) .
From among you is the Qa’im, behind whom Jesus son of Mary will pray when God sends him down to the earth. He is from the descendants of Ali and Fatimah, from the line of al-Husayn.

quotes.caption: Imam al-Hasan, Ithbat al-Hudat, vol. 5, p. 81, report 118

paragraphs.text: 118 - وقال : حدثنا المظفر بن جعفر العلوي عن جعفر بن محمّد بن مسعود عن أبيه عن جبرئيل بن أحمد عن موسى بن جعفر البغدادي عن الحسن بن محمّد الصيرفي عن حنان بن سدير عن أبيه عن أبي سعيد عقيصا عن الحسن بن علي ﵇ في حديث قال : أما علمتم أنه ما منا أحد إلا وتقع في عنقه بيعة لطاغية زمانه إلا القائم الذي يصلّي عيسى بن مريم خلفه ، وإن اللّه ﷿ يخفي ولادته ويغيب شخصه لئلا يكون لأحد في عنقه بيعة إذا خرج ذلك التاسع من ولد أخي الحسين ابن سيدة النساء يطيل اللّه عمره في غيبته ثم يظهره بقدرته في صورة شاب ابن دون أربعين سنة ليعلم أن اللّه على كل شيء قدير (4) .

He said, "Al-Muzaffar ibn Jafar al-Alawi narrated to us, from Jafar ibn Muhammad ibn Masud, from his father, from Jibril ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Jafar al-Baghdadi, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad al-Sayrafi, from Hannan ibn Sudayr, from his father, from Abu Said Uqaysa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, in a report in which he said,
'Do you not know that there is none of us except that allegiance to the tyrant of his time falls upon his neck, except the Qa'im, behind whom Jesus son of Mary will pray?

Allah conceals his birth and hides his person so that no one's allegiance may be upon his neck when he emerges. That ninth one from the descendants of my brother al-Husayn, son of the Lady of Women, Allah will prolong his life during his occultation, then He will manifest him by His power in the form of a young man under forty years old, so that it may be known that Allah has power over all things.'"

source_review.reviewer: Codex preparation with actual independent prose/source reviews; hosted final release pending

blocks.text: The Sun, the Moon, and Twelve Stars
blocks.observation: “The Sun, the Moon, and Twelve Stars”: Names the celestial image without promising proof or narrating a method.

blocks.text: Imami reports associate the sun and moon with Muhammad and Ali, count twelve Imams, and describe the Mahdi as a ruler of justice. Later writers use these reports to interpret Revelation 12 and other biblical passages.
blocks.observation: “Imami reports associate the sun and moon with Muhammad and Ali, count”: Separates early symbolic traditions from later biblical applications; gives the subject directly.

blocks.text: # The Sun, the Moon, and Twelve Stars
blocks.observation: “# The Sun, the Moon, and Twelve Stars”: Visible title repeats metadata for display, not a body argument.

blocks.text: 1. Revelation 12:1 describes a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon beneath her feet and a crown of twelve stars. Genesis 17:20 promises Ishmael twelve princes. Isaiah 11:1-9, Psalm 72, and Daniel 7:13-14 describe righteous rule and dominion.
blocks.observation: “1. Revelation 12:1 describes a woman clothed with the sun, with the”: Verse locators give the three comparison subjects without methodological praise.

blocks.text: 2. The Qur'an swears by a sun and by a moon that follows it (Qur'an 91:1-2), and the Imams' transmitted tafsir names that sun as the Prophet ﷺ and that moon as Ali ﵇.
blocks.observation: “2. The Qur'an swears by a sun and by a moon that”: The moon-following relation supplies the basis of the attributed Imami interpretation.

blocks.text: 3. Shia and Sunni collections report twelve successors, and a report cited from Ahmad's Musnad compares their number with the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel. Imami reports name Ali as the first Imam and the Mahdi as the last; eleven of the twelve are Fatimah's descendants.
blocks.observation: “3. Shia and Sunni collections report twelve successors, and a report cited”: Named Imami sequence stays distinct from shared count; eleven descendants preserves the numerical qualification.

blocks.text: 4. Sunni reports identify a Mahdi descended from Fatimah ﵍ and separately describe Jesus's ﵇ descent with an imam from the Muslim community. The quoted Imami reports expressly identify the leader behind whom Jesus prays as the Mahdi or Qa'im.
blocks.observation: “4. Sunni reports identify a Mahdi descended from Fatimah ﵍ and separately”: Separate Sunni descent and Imami prayer claims prevent conflation; this carries evidence rather than decorative contrast.

blocks.text: ## The Facts
blocks.observation: “## The Facts”: Labels the required evidence catalogue without adding a prose thesis.

blocks.text: | Claim | Actor | Date | Place | Source | Qualifier | ↗ |
blocks.observation: “| Claim | Actor | Date | Place | Source | Qualifier”: Columns distinguish statement, attribution, time, source, and qualification.

blocks.text: | The Imams after me are twelve, the first of them Ali and the last of them al-Qa'im | The Prophet ﷺ, reported through al-Sadiq, his father, and his grandfather | 1st century AH, attributed | not stated | Kamal al-Din, p. 289, report 4 | attributed | [[#Twelve Imams in their own reports|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| The Imams after me are twelve, the first of them Ali”: Actor follows displayed Kamal chain through al-Sadiq, father, and grandfather; Ali is no longer misidentified as transmitter.

blocks.text: | Twelve caliphs, all from Quraysh; the Musnad report ties the number to the nuqaba, the twelve chiefs, of the Children of Israel | The Prophet ﷺ, reported by Jabir b. Samura and Ibn Mas'ud; the latter report is transmitted by Masruq | 1st century AH, attributed | not stated | Sahih Muslim; Ahadith al-Mahdi min Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, p. 43, citing Musnad Ahmad, vol. 1, p. 398; Sunan Abi Dawud 4279-4282 | reported | [[#Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| Twelve caliphs, all from Quraysh; the Musnad report ties the number”: Masruq is distinguished as transmitter of Ibn Masud’s report; count and genealogy remain explicit.

blocks.text: | The sun of Qur'an 91 is the Prophet ﷺ and its moon is Ali ﵇ | Imam al-Sadiq ﵇, reported by Abu Basir; al-Husayn ﵇, in Furat’s report | 1st to 2nd centuries AH, attributed | not stated | Tafsir al-Qummi, vol. 2, p. 424; Tafsir Furat al-Kufi, p. 563; al-Kafi | attributed | [[#An oath by the sun and the moon|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “The sun of Qur'an 91 is the Prophet”: the actor cell distinguishes al-Sadiq and al-Husayn; the date now spans first to second centuries AH and no longer assigns both to the second century. This resolves the date handoff as an editorial attribution issue.

blocks.text: | I am the sun, Ali is the moon, Fatimah is Venus, and the two Farqads are Hasan and Husayn | The Prophet ﷺ, reported by Anas and Jabir | 1st century AH, attributed | not stated | Ma'ani al-Akhbar, pp. 208-209; Nuzhat al-Majalis, vol. 2, p. 315 | attributed | [[#The lights of one house|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| I am the sun, Ali is the moon, Fatimah is Venus,”: Venus and Farqads identities are essential to the later twelve-star mapping difficulty.

blocks.text: | The woman of Revelation 12 is Fatimah ﵍ | Al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri, the author's own reading | 14th century AH | not stated | Ilzam al-Nasib, vol. 1, pp. 129-130 | stated | [[#The Fatimah reading and its history|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| The woman of Revelation 12 is Fatimah ﵍ | Al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri,”: Fatimah identification is al-Hairi’s reading rather than an Imam’s transmitted exegesis.

blocks.text: | Ishmael's twelve princes are the twelve Imams ﵈ | Al-Nu'mani, from a named Jewish scholar's Torah reading | 4th century AH | Arrajan | Kitab al-Ghayba, p. 108 | reported | [[#Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| Ishmael's twelve princes are the twelve Imams ﵈ | Al-Nu'mani, from”: Jewish scholar intermediary preserves actual attribution instead of implying direct Imam transmission.

blocks.text: | The Mahdi is from the Prophet's progeny, from the children of Fatimah ﵍, and fills the earth with justice | The Prophet ﷺ, reported by Umm Salama and Abu Sa'id | 1st century AH, attributed | not stated | Sunan Abi Dawud 4284-4285 | attributed | [[#The ruler who fills the earth with justice|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| The Mahdi is from the Prophet's progeny, from the children of”: Fatimah lineage and justice supply concrete features for the comparison.

blocks.text: | Jesus ﵇ descends, and the Muslims' imam is from among them | The Prophet ﷺ, reported by Abu Hurayra | 1st century AH, attributed | not stated | Ahadith al-Mahdi min Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal, p. 64, report 97, citing Musnad Ahmad, vol. 2, p. 336 | reported | [[#The ruler who fills the earth with justice|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| Jesus ﵇ descends, and the Muslims' imam is from among them”: Sunni row leaves imam unnamed in its claim and identifies Abu Hurayra transmission.

blocks.text: | Jesus ﵇ prays behind the Mahdi or Qa'im | Reports attributed to the Prophet ﷺ, Imam al-Rida ﵇, and Imam al-Hasan ﵇ | 1st to 3rd centuries AH, attributed | not stated | al-Kafi, vol. 8, pp. 73-74; Uyun Akhbar al-Rida, vol. 2, pp. 217-218; Ithbat al-Hudat, vol. 5, p. 81 | reported | [[#The ruler who fills the earth with justice|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| Jesus ﵇ prays behind the Mahdi or Qa'im | Reports attributed”: Separate Imami row explicitly names Mahdi/Qaim and preserves attributed speakers.

blocks.text: | The woman of Revelation 12 is read as Mary, as the Church, or as Israel | Pius XII; the Catholic Encyclopedia's authors | 1950 and 1907 | not stated | Munificentissimus Deus 27; Catholic Encyclopedia, Apocalypse | stated | [[#Catholic readings of the woman|↗]] |
blocks.observation: “| The woman of Revelation 12 is read as Mary, as the”: Lists Catholic alternatives with sources; no ironic dismissal of disagreement.

blocks.text: ## Biblical images and the Prophet's family
blocks.observation: “## Biblical images and the Prophet's family”: Names comparison without opening with a defensive denial.

blocks.text: Revelation 12 and Genesis 17 do not name Muhammad ﷺ, Ali ﵇, Fatimah ﵍, or the twelve Imams. Identifying the biblical figures with members of the Prophet's family depends on parallels with Islamic reports.
blocks.observation: “Revelation 12 and Genesis 17 do not name Muhammad ﷺ, Ali ﵇,”: Books and figures now have explicit referents; naming limit remains necessary.

blocks.text: ## A woman clothed with the sun
blocks.observation: “## A woman clothed with the sun”: Locates Revelation’s image directly before its source quotation.

blocks.text: In Revelation 12:1, the Arabic transcription quoted here has a form meaning “his wife”; the archived Smith-Van Dyck text reads “a woman.” The Greek and English printed here also read “a woman.”
blocks.observation: “In Revelation 12:1, the Arabic transcription quoted here”: wife/woman difference is a substantive source variant, not editorial process leakage. Smith-Van Dyck spelling changed only the source-name typography; its meaning and concise explanation remain intact.

blocks.text: The woman's child is taken to God and his throne. The dragon then attacks her remaining offspring, who keep God's commandments and bear witness to Jesus.
blocks.observation: “The woman's child is taken to God and his throne. The dragon”: States child removal and dragon attack with clear actors, useful when callouts are collapsed.

blocks.text: Revelation 12:9 identifies the dragon as Satan.
blocks.observation: “Revelation 12:9 identifies the dragon as Satan.”: Adds Satan identification and precise verse beyond other quoted verses.

blocks.text: ## Catholic readings of the woman
blocks.observation: “## Catholic readings of the woman”: Scopes sources to Catholic interpretations without claiming all Christianity.

blocks.text: Pope Pius XII, defining the Assumption of Mary in 1950, wrote that the scholastic doctors recognized the Assumption as signified in "that woman clothed with the sun whom John the Apostle contemplated on the Island of Patmos" (Munificentissimus Deus 27). The Catholic Encyclopedia states, "The woman in travail is a personification of the synagogue or the church. Her first-born is Christ, her other seed is the community of the faithful" (Van den Biesen, "Apocalypse," 1907). The same article connects the sun, moon, and twelve stars with Joseph's dream in Genesis 37:9-10.
blocks.observation: “Pope Pius XII, defining the Assumption of Mary in 1950, wrote that”: Pius and Encyclopedia are individually attributed; Genesis cross-reference supplies textual basis for comparison.

blocks.text: In Joseph's dream, the sun, moon, and eleven stars bow to him (Genesis 37:9-10). Revelation has twelve stars and depicts a woman with a child.
blocks.observation: “In Joseph's dream, the sun, moon, and eleven stars bow to him”: Eleven versus twelve stars is a real textual difference, not an ornamental contrast.

blocks.text: ## An oath by the sun and the moon
blocks.observation: “## An oath by the sun and the moon”: Names Quranic oath without announcing an argumentative turn.

blocks.text: In the moon clause, tala means “to follow.” Al-Qummi transmits Abu Basir's report of al-Sadiq's interpretation.
blocks.observation: “In the moon clause, tala means “to follow.” Al-Qummi transmits Abu Basir's”: Defines tala and identifies al-Qummi’s transmission without overclaiming unanimous school doctrine.

blocks.text: In the report transmitted by al-Qummi, al-Sadiq identifies the sun with Muhammad ﷺ and the moon with Ali ﵇. The day represents an Imam from Fatimah's descendants who explains the Prophet's religion. Furat transmits a report attributed to al-Husayn that identifies the day specifically with the Qa'im, the Imam who will fill the earth with justice.
blocks.observation: “In the report transmitted by al-Qummi, al-Sadiq identifies the sun with Muhammad”: Distinguishes day-as-Imam from day-as-Qaim; comparison explains a substantive variant.

blocks.text: Al-Kafi also transmits the sun-and-moon interpretation in its Rawda volume. Furat preserves versions attributed to Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Shahrashub includes related interpretations attributed to al-Baqir and al-Sadiq. Ta'wil al-Ayat preserves a different interpretation.
blocks.observation: “Al-Kafi also transmits the sun-and-moon interpretation in its Rawda volume. Furat preserves”: Identifies additional attributed versions and introduces Ta’wil’s alternate assignment once.

blocks.text: In this version, the sun is Ali ﵇, the moon represents al-Hasan and al-Husayn ﵈, and the heaven is Muhammad ﷺ. Al-Astarabadi transmits it through two chains in Ta'wil al-Ayat. Al-Burhan and Bihar al-Anwar reproduce his report.
blocks.observation: “In this version, the sun is Ali ﵇, the moon represents al-Hasan”: Preserves alternate sun/moon assignments and source dependence; redundant source inventory is gone.

blocks.text: ## The lights of one house
blocks.observation: “## The lights of one house”: Names household imagery without theatrical evaluation of its strength.

blocks.text: A report in al-Saduq's Ma'ani al-Akhbar associates Venus with Fatimah and the two Farqads with Hasan and Husayn.
blocks.observation: “A report in al-Saduq's Ma'ani al-Akhbar associates Venus with Fatimah and the”: Adds Venus and Farqads to previously discussed sun and moon.

blocks.text: Al-Safuri includes the report in Nuzhat al-Majalis, citing Ara'is. Ibn Shahrashub also attributes it to al-Natanzi's al-Khasa'is.
blocks.observation: “Al-Safuri includes the report in Nuzhat al-Majalis, citing Ara'is. Ibn Shahrashub also”: Indirect al-Natanzi attribution is explicit through Ibn Shahrashub, avoiding false direct-consultation claim.

blocks.text: In Salman's report, transmitted by al-Khazzaz, the shining stars are nine Imams descended from al-Husayn.
blocks.observation: “In Salman's report, transmitted by al-Khazzaz, the shining stars are nine Imams”: States nine later Imams before longer source, giving reader its numerical premise.

blocks.text: Salman's report lists twelve successors and compares their number with Jacob's tribes and Jesus's apostles. Its celestial images distinguish Ali as the moon, Hasan and Husayn as the two Farqads, and nine later Imams as shining stars. Revelation instead gives the woman a crown of twelve stars. Identifying that crown with all twelve Imams therefore assigns Ali a place among the stars as well as the moon. The quoted Islamic reports do not make that identification.
blocks.observation: “Salman's report lists twelve successors and compares their number with Jacob's tribes”: Explains Ali’s double symbolic role in twelve-star identification; preserves report’s silence on that identification.

blocks.text: Al-Qummi's report from al-Baqir interprets Joseph's dream through Joseph's own family.
blocks.observation: “Al-Qummi's report from al-Baqir interprets Joseph's dream through Joseph's own family.”: Identifies Joseph-family interpretation instead of making a universal absence claim.

blocks.text: The sun represents Joseph's mother, the moon Jacob, and the eleven stars his brothers.
blocks.observation: “The sun represents Joseph's mother, the moon Jacob, and the eleven stars”: Gives actual mother/father/brothers mapping for readers who keep long callout collapsed.

blocks.text: ## The Fatimah reading and its history
blocks.observation: “## The Fatimah reading and its history”: Names later Fatimah interpretation and history without asserting earliest provenance.

blocks.text: Baydun describes the crown as Fatimah's twelve infallible sons, beginning with Hasan and Husayn. The Imami sequence quoted here contains eleven of her descendants and her husband, Ali, so his wording does not match that count. Baydun cites chapter 11 for a quotation from Revelation 12:1. Al-Yazdi al-Ha'iri gives a longer interpretation in Ilzam al-Nasib. His paraphrase includes mountains being lowered and rough places made smooth, clauses absent from Revelation 12.
blocks.observation: “Baydun describes the crown as Fatimah's twelve infallible sons, beginning with Hasan”: Count mismatch and extra Revelation clauses are direct qualifications; Baydun chapter correction is now adjacent to his claim.

blocks.text: Al-Ha'iri identifies the dragon with Banu Umayyah, the child with the hidden Qa'im, and the iron rod with his sword. He rejects the identification of the child with Jesus on the ground that Jesus never fought. In his other mapping, Muhammad, Ali, and ten descendants form the twelve stars, and the Qa'im is the moon.
blocks.observation: “Al-Ha'iri identifies the dragon with Banu Umayyah, the child with the hidden”: Attributes Jesus-never-fought objection to al-Hairi and separates alternate mapping rather than adopting either as fact.

blocks.text: ## Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael
blocks.observation: “## Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael”: Names Ishmael’s twelve-prince promise; seed is ordinary scriptural terminology here.

blocks.text: Islamic genealogy traces Muhammad ﷺ to Ishmael. Al-Nu'mani records an interpretation connecting Ishmael's twelve princes with twelve Imams.
blocks.observation: “Islamic genealogy traces Muhammad ﷺ to Ishmael. Al-Nu'mani records an interpretation connecting”: Gives genealogy and al-Numani’s interpretation without claiming earliest or strongest transmission.

blocks.text: Al-Rawandi also relates the blessing of Ishmael to Muhammad ﷺ.
blocks.observation: “Al-Rawandi also relates the blessing of Ishmael to Muhammad ﷺ.”: Related Rawandi gloss adds distinct source without ranking its evidentiary strength.

blocks.text: Majlisi, writing in the seventeenth century, says he heard the Hebrew passage read and translated by People of the Book whom he trusted.
blocks.observation: “Majlisi, writing in the seventeenth century, says he heard the Hebrew passage”: Majlisi’s trust judgment belongs to Majlisi, not the article as independent certification.

blocks.text: Majlisi says that the reports suggest that “Madmad” is Muhammad's ﷺ name in Hebrew. Bihar also transmits a narrative in which Abraham is told that Muhammad's family will descend from his firstborn, Ishmael.
blocks.observation: “Majlisi says that the reports suggest that “Madmad” is Muhammad's ﷺ name”: Reports suggest retains Majlisi’s tentative inference; Abraham narrative is separately attributed.

blocks.text: Majlisi quotes this narrative from Ibn Tawus's Iqbal al-A'mal. Ibn Tawus names Abu al-Mufaddal al-Shaybani's book on the mutual imprecation and al-Hasan ibn Isma'il ibn Ashnas's work on the observances of Dhu al-Hijja among his sources.
blocks.observation: “Majlisi quotes this narrative from Ibn Tawus's Iqbal al-A'mal. Ibn Tawus names”: Provides named provenance without an unsourced dismissal of compiler character.

blocks.text: Genesis 25:13-16 identifies twelve princes as Ishmael's sons. Al-Nu'mani's application to the Imams treats the promise as extending to later descendants of Ishmael. He reports a Jewish scholar's dictation transmitted to him through Abd al-Halim ibn al-Husayn al-Samuri; this passage gives no chain to an Imam.
blocks.observation: “Genesis 25:13-16 identifies twelve princes as Ishmael's sons. Al-Nu'mani's application to the”: Genesis’s sons and extension to later descendants are distinguished; no-chain limit is specific, not litotes.

blocks.text: ## Twelve Imams in their own reports
blocks.observation: “## Twelve Imams in their own reports”: Own-reports denotes attributed Imami reports, not an opponent’s own admission.

blocks.text: Al-Kafi reports that Jabir saw a tablet in Fatimah's hands naming members of her family and their successors.
blocks.observation: “Al-Kafi reports that Jabir saw a tablet in Fatimah's hands naming members”: Tablet narrative is reported by al-Kafi rather than asserted as independently established history.

blocks.text: According to the Tablet report, Jabir copied its text and al-Baqir recited it in agreement with his copy. The text describes a sequence of successors ending with “Mim Ha Mim Dal,” the letters of the name Muhammad. Versions also appear in al-Saduq's Kamal al-Din and Uyun Akhbar al-Rida; al-Hurr al-Amili additionally lists a version in al-Tusi's Ghayba.
blocks.observation: “According to the Tablet report, Jabir copied its text and al-Baqir recited”: Four letter names are explained as Muhammad; copying comparison and later attestations remain attributed.

blocks.text: Al-Hurr al-Amili notes that al-Khazzaz transmits this report from Ibn Babawayh through the same chain.
blocks.observation: “Al-Hurr al-Amili notes that al-Khazzaz transmits this report from Ibn Babawayh through”: Shared chain through Ibn Babawayh states dependence, not independent corroboration.

blocks.text: Al-Saduq cites reports transmitted by Sunni traditionists as support for the Imami count of twelve.
blocks.observation: “Al-Saduq cites reports transmitted by Sunni traditionists as support for the Imami”: States al-Saduq’s use of Sunni reports once before quotation.

blocks.text: The nuqaba are the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel. A report in al-Kafi also compares Muhammad's twelve trustees with the twelve trustees of Jesus.
blocks.observation: “The nuqaba are the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel. A”: Defines nuqaba and adds Jesus-trustee comparison; repeated al-Saduq statement was deleted.

blocks.text: Another report in al-Kafi attributes the succession testimony to a visitor whom Ali ﵇ identifies as al-Khidr. He names the first eleven Imams and identifies the twelfth by descent.
blocks.observation: “Another report in al-Kafi attributes the succession testimony to a visitor whom”: Eleven named Imams and twelfth by descent preserve distinct identifying forms in testimony.

blocks.text: A kunyah is a byname such as Abu so-and-so. The report says that the twelfth is neither named nor called by a kunyah until his affair becomes manifest.
blocks.observation: “A kunyah is a byname such as Abu so-and-so. The report says”: Defines kunyah and preserves naming restriction without former publicly-no-one embellishment.

blocks.text: ## Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon
blocks.observation: “## Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon”: Locates Sunni collection section without praising its argument.

blocks.text: Sahih Muslim transmits Jabir ibn Samura's report of twelve caliphs from Quraysh through several chains.
blocks.observation: “Sahih Muslim transmits Jabir ibn Samura's report of twelve caliphs from Quraysh”: Identifies Muslim’s transmitted count without unsupported strongest-chain grade.

blocks.text: The anthology Ahadith al-Mahdi min Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal transmits Ibn Mas'ud's report comparing twelve caliphs with the twelve chiefs of the Children of Israel, citing Musnad Ahmad, vol. 1, p. 398.
blocks.observation: “The anthology Ahadith al-Mahdi min Musnad Ahmad ibn Hanbal transmits Ibn Mas'ud's”: Distinguishes consulted anthology from cited Ahmad volume, a meaningful provenance detail.

blocks.text: In Abu Dawud's chapter on the Mahdi, the quoted report gives the ruler's father the Prophet's father's name. This does not match the Imami identification of the Mahdi as the son of al-Hasan. Al-Kanji, as quoted in Sharh Ihqaq al-Haqq, discusses attempts to reconcile the clause, calls that interpretation strained, and appeals to Ahmad's transmissions without it (vol. 33, pp. 943-944).
blocks.observation: “In Abu Dawud's chapter on the Mahdi, the quoted report gives the”: Father-name discrepancy is substantive; al-Kanji assessment is attributed through consulted Sharh.

blocks.text: Al-Nawawi quotes al-Qadi Iyad's distinction between the thirty years of prophetic caliphate and the twelve rulers, for whom no such condition is stated. Al-Qadi also argues that a prediction of twelve rulers permits later rulers. Kanz al-Ummal transmits a report attributed to Ibn Abbas. It places al-Mansur, al-Saffah, and the Mahdi after twelve commanders. The Mahdi would then hand authority to Jesus.
blocks.observation: “Al-Nawawi quotes al-Qadi Iyad's distinction between the thirty years of prophetic caliphate”: States al-Qadi’s two answers directly and keeps Kanz future succession attributed.

blocks.text: ## The king who reigns in righteousness
blocks.observation: “## The king who reigns in righteousness”: Names righteous royal rule without assuming all passages name the same ruler.

blocks.text: Isaiah 32:1 describes a king who reigns in righteousness, with princes who rule in judgment.
blocks.observation: “Isaiah 32:1 describes a king who reigns in righteousness, with princes who”: Adds Isaiah32:1, a precise verse outside earlier full block quotations.

blocks.text: Before Pilate, Jesus ﵇ says that his kingdom is not from this world and that his servants are not fighting to prevent his surrender. This statement does not exclude a future reign on earth. On a reading that requires worldwide peace and a public reign of justice, the prophetic promises extend beyond the events of Jesus's earthly ministry.
blocks.observation: “Before Pilate, Jesus ﵇ says that his kingdom is not from this”: Does-not-exclude retains John’s logical limit; literal-public reading is expressly a premise, not universal Christian doctrine.

blocks.text: Van den Biesen affirms Christ's future return. He also presents Augustine's interpretation of Revelation's thousand-year reign as the Church's present spiritual life (Catholic Encyclopedia, “Apocalypse,” 1907, “Purpose of the book”).
blocks.observation: “Van den Biesen affirms Christ's future return. He also presents Augustine's interpretation”: Defines millennium as Revelation’s thousand-year reign; attributes spiritual reading to Augustine through Van den Biesen.

blocks.text: | Passage | What it promises |
blocks.observation: “| Passage | What it promises |”: Two columns separate passage from substantive promise without repetitive paraphrase column.

blocks.text: | Isaiah 2:2-4, Micah 4:1-4 | God judges among the nations; weapons become farming tools, and nations cease learning war |
blocks.observation: “| Isaiah 2:2-4, Micah 4:1-4 | God judges among the nations; weapons”: Keeps concrete judgments, agricultural tools, and cessation of war once.

blocks.text: | Isaiah 11:1-9 | A ruler from Jesse's line judges the poor and slays the wicked; there is freedom from harm on the holy mountain, and the earth is full of the knowledge of God |
blocks.observation: “| Isaiah 11:1-9 | A ruler from Jesse's line judges the poor”: Retains worldwide knowledge and holy-mountain protection rather than broadening the latter globally.

blocks.text: | Jeremiah 23:5-8, 33:14-16 | A righteous Branch from David's line executes justice, and Israel returns to its land. Judah is saved, Israel dwells safely in chapter 23, and Jerusalem dwells safely in chapter 33 |
blocks.observation: “| Jeremiah 23:5-8, 33:14-16 | A righteous Branch from David's line executes”: Distinguishes Israel/Jerusalem across chapters and retains return to land from removed third column.

blocks.text: | Ezekiel 37:21-28 | Israel is gathered into one nation under David as king and shepherd, with God's sanctuary among them forever |
blocks.observation: “| Ezekiel 37:21-28 | Israel is gathered into one nation under David”: Preserves reunification, Davidic rule, and lasting sanctuary in a single description.

blocks.text: | Hosea 3:5 | Israel returns and seeks the Lord and David their king in the latter days |
blocks.observation: “| Hosea 3:5 | Israel returns and seeks the Lord and David”: Latter days remains text’s timing qualification without another cell repeating it.

blocks.text: | Psalm 72 | The king judges the poor, crushes the oppressor, rules to the ends of the earth, and brings abundance and peace while the moon endures |
blocks.observation: “| Psalm 72 | The king judges the poor, crushes the oppressor,”: Preserves justice, oppression, dominion, abundance, and source moon-duration phrase.

blocks.text: | Daniel 2:44, 7:13-14, 7:27 | God establishes an enduring kingdom that displaces the kingdoms in the vision; one like a son of man receives dominion, and the holy people receive the kingdom |
blocks.observation: “| Daniel 2:44, 7:13-14, 7:27 | God establishes an enduring kingdom that”: Retains displaced kingdoms, son-of-man dominion, and holy people receiving kingdom without unsupported Rome identification.

blocks.text: ## The ruler who fills the earth with justice
blocks.observation: “## The ruler who fills the earth with justice”: Names actual justice theme of Mahdi reports.

blocks.text: Reports in Sunan Abi Dawud describe the Mahdi as a descendant of Fatimah who will fill the earth with justice.
blocks.observation: “Reports in Sunan Abi Dawud describe the Mahdi as a descendant of”: States exact lineage and justice features used in comparison.

blocks.text: A report in Ibn al-Munadi's al-Malahim describes equal distribution of wealth during the Mahdi's reign.
blocks.observation: “A report in Ibn al-Munadi's al-Malahim describes equal distribution of wealth during”: Equal distribution introduces distinct economic content, not a generic source announcement.

blocks.text: Psalm 72 describes a king who judges the poor, defeats oppressors, and brings abundance and peace. The Mahdi reports likewise describe justice and material sufficiency.
blocks.observation: “Psalm 72 describes a king who judges the poor, defeats oppressors, and”: Short comparison relates Psalm72 justice/abundance to Mahdi reports without job-description refrain.

blocks.text: The report attributed to Ahmad leaves the imam unnamed. The Imami report attributed to Ibn Abbas identifies the Mahdi as the last of twelve successors and says that Jesus will pray behind him.
blocks.observation: “The report attributed to Ahmad leaves the imam unnamed. The Imami report”: Named/unnamed distinction prevents treating Sunni and Imami reports as identical evidence.

blocks.text: Uyun Akhbar al-Rida attributes the same prediction of Jesus praying behind the Mahdi to al-Rida in a discussion with al-Ma'mun.
blocks.observation: “Uyun Akhbar al-Rida attributes the same prediction of Jesus praying behind the”: Al-Mamun setting locates al-Rida prediction without paraphrasing entire source again.

blocks.text: In the report attributed to al-Hasan, God conceals the Qa'im's birth so that he will owe no allegiance to the ruler of his time when he emerges.
blocks.observation: “In the report attributed to al-Hasan, God conceals the Qa'im's birth so”: Concealed birth’s stated purpose is attributed and avoids adopting source first-person voice.

blocks.text: Isaiah 11 describes a ruler from Jesse's line, and Jeremiah 23 names David's line. The Mahdi reports quoted here identify him through Muhammad's ﷺ and Fatimah's ﵍ line. The Imami prediction that Jesus ﵇ will pray behind the Mahdi distinguishes the two figures, but it does not identify the Mahdi as David's descendant or explicitly assign him every office described in these biblical passages.
blocks.observation: “Isaiah 11 describes a ruler from Jesse's line, and Jeremiah 23 names”: Davidic descent remains unresolved scope limit; prayer leadership is not expanded to every biblical office.

blocks.text: ## Final Verdict
blocks.observation: “## Final Verdict”: Retains required category-close label without rhetorical heading flourish.

blocks.text: These biblical passages and Imami reports share celestial imagery, a count of twelve, and descriptions of just rule. Applying the biblical figures to Fatimah ﵍, the Imams, and the Mahdi remains an interpretation. The twelve-star crown differs from the Islamic reports' distribution of symbols, Genesis identifies Ishmael's twelve princes as his sons, and Isaiah and Jeremiah specify Jesse's or David's line.
blocks.observation: “These biblical passages and Imami reports share celestial imagery, a count of”: Shortened ending gives comparison and three essential limits; redundant prayer-report pair is gone.

The final prose pass preserves the unnamed Sunni imam, Imami identification, eleven descendants plus Ali, literal sons in Genesis, and unresolved Davidic lineage.

Source adjudicator found no remaining blocking fidelity defects within documented scope; report-chain authenticity is not established.

The hosted reviewer required FID-14, now corrected from after it to after him against the retained source page; final hosted approval is still pending.

advisors.response:
### P-01
**Section:** Front matter summary

**Exact sentence:** “Revelation's woman, Ishmael's twelve princes, and the Bible's reigning king of justice converge, by job description rather than by name, on Fatimah, the twelve Imams, and the Mahdi.”

**Defect class:** Vague abstraction; overstated convergence.

**Contribution:** States the article’s thesis and distinguishes identification by function from identification by name.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve that the article compares three biblical descriptions with Islamic reports and argues for correspondences rather than explicit biblical naming. Do not say the figures “converge” before distinguishing the different evidentiary strength of the three correspondences.

---

### P-02
**Section:** Abstract

**Exact sentences:** “The conclusion is weighed, not named. The Bible's unnamed figures and the Islamic corpus's named figures carry the same assignments, so the Bible supplies the job description and the Islamic reports supply the identity.”

**Defect class:** Decorative contrast; personification; repeated slogan.

**Contribution:** Qualifies the conclusion as an inference and summarizes the proposed division between biblical descriptions and Islamic identifications.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve that the biblical texts do not name the figures and that the proposed identifications depend on comparing their described roles with Islamic reports. Remove “weighed, not named,” “carry,” “supplies,” and the slogan-like parallel structure.

---

### P-03
**Section:** No verse names the house

**Exact sentence:** “A claim that the Bible ‘contains’ the Prophet's family by name would fail on its face, and no honest case would make it.”

**Defect class:** Argumentative theater; moral certification of the author’s position.

**Contribution:** Rejects the stronger claim that the Bible explicitly names the Ahl al-Bayt.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve only the textual limitation: none of the cited biblical passages names Muhammad, Ali, Fatimah, or the Imams. Delete the judgment about what an “honest case” would do.

---

### P-04
**Section:** No verse names the house

**Exact sentence:** “That question can be answered without forcing a single verse.”

**Defect class:** Empty meta-commentary; self-certification.

**Contribution:** Claims that the ensuing interpretation respects the texts.

**Action:** **Delete.** The article must demonstrate that restraint through its comparisons and qualifications. The sentence adds no evidence or reasoning.

---

### P-05
**Section:** No verse names the house

**Exact sentence:** “If those reports carry the Tradition's own astral code and its own count, then the Bible's woman, its twelve princes, and its reigning king describe a configuration the Islamic sources had already assembled under names.”

**Defect class:** Vague abstraction; theatrical personification; metaphor substituted for the precise inference.

**Contribution:** Draws the section’s central inference from the Islamic astral interpretations, the number twelve, and the Mahdi reports.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the conditional inference by naming its parts directly: if the cited Islamic reports identify the sun and moon, specify twelve successors, and describe the final just ruler, those reports provide proposed identities for the otherwise unnamed biblical figures. Avoid “astral code,” “configuration,” and sources “assembling” it.

---

### P-06
**Section:** No verse names the house

**Exact sentences:** “The method has a limit that the closing section states exactly. A match of assignments is a reading, and a reading can be weighed.”

**Defect class:** Internal article narration; empty meta-commentary; vague abstraction.

**Contribution:** Introduces a necessary limitation on the argument.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the limitation itself and state it here directly: similarity of roles supports an interpretation but does not establish an explicit prophecy or uniquely identify its subject. Delete the reference to what the closing section will do.

---

### P-07
**Section:** Who the churches say she is

**Exact sentence:** “So the standard Christian identifications are Mary, the Church, and Israel, and one mainstream Catholic reference itself concedes that the woman's sun, moon, and stars come from Joseph's dream, in which the sun and the moon and eleven stars bow to one of Jacob's sons (Genesis 37:9).”

**Defect class:** Source-as-performance narration; adversarial diction.

**Contribution:** Records the three Christian identifications and the Catholic Encyclopedia’s Genesis 37 cross-reference.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve both facts, but replace “itself concedes” with neutral attribution: the Catholic Encyclopedia connects the imagery to Joseph’s dream in Genesis 37:9–10.

---

### P-08
**Section:** Who the churches say she is

**Exact sentences:** “None of these readings is a fact about the text. Each is an assignment, and the assignment has to fit the figure's relations. A woman whose sign is a sun she wears, a moon under her feet, and twelve stars as her crown must be a woman whose household is the sun, the moon, and the twelve.”

**Defect class:** Vague abstraction; unjustified modal force; rhetorical restatement.

**Contribution:** Distinguishes explicit textual content from proposed identification and states the criterion used by the argument.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve that the text does not identify the woman and that any interpretation must explain her relation to the sun, moon, and twelve stars. Replace “must be” and “whose household is” with the narrower claim that the article tests whether an identified woman has intelligible relations to figures represented by those signs.

---

### P-09
**Section:** An oath by the sun and the moon

**Exact sentences:** “In the school of the Ahl al-Bayt this oath was read through the Imams' own words, and the reading answers the question directly. Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi records it with a full chain.”

**Defect class:** Source-as-performance narration; vague evaluative claim.

**Contribution:** Attributes the interpretation and introduces its chain of transmission.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve that al-Qummi transmits, through a stated chain, a report attributing the interpretation to Imam al-Sadiq. Delete “answers the question directly,” which evaluates before presenting the evidence.

---

### P-10
**Section:** An oath by the sun and the moon

**Exact sentences:** “So yes. In the Imami transmission the sun of the oath is the Prophet and its moon is Ali, and the day is the Qa'im who fills the earth with justice. The reading is not a single stray voice.”

**Defect class:** Empty emphatic fragment; litotes; source-as-performance narration.

**Contribution:** Summarizes the reported identifications and notes that they occur in more than one source.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Delete “So yes” and “not a single stray voice.” Preserve the identifications and state the actual evidence directly: the article cites corresponding reports in al-Kafi, al-Qummi, Furat, and Ibn Shahrashub, while later acknowledging a variant.

---

### P-11
**Section:** An oath by the sun and the moon

**Exact sentence:** “One recorded variant assigns the figures differently, and honesty requires stating it.”

**Defect class:** Self-certification; research-performance narration.

**Contribution:** Introduces relevant counterevidence.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve only the evidentiary point: “One recorded variant assigns the figures differently.” The quotation and subsequent analysis establish why it matters.

---

### P-12
**Section:** An oath by the sun and the moon

**Exact sentence:** “Within the Imami school itself, the dominant reading of the oath is the one the woman of Revelation 12 would need.”

**Defect class:** Argumentative theater; personification of the proposed interpretation; vague evidentiary ranking.

**Contribution:** Claims that the better-attested Imami interpretation supplies the sun-and-moon identification required by the Fatimah reading.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the comparative claim only if “dominant” is source-supported: the more widely carried version identifies the sun as Muhammad and the moon as Ali, which is the version used in the article’s proposed comparison with Revelation 12.

---

### P-13
**Section:** The lights of one house

**Exact sentence:** “The Tradition does not leave the sun and the moon as a pair.”

**Defect class:** Theatrical personification; empty quotation introduction.

**Contribution:** Announces that subsequent reports add Fatimah, Hasan, Husayn, and the remaining Imams to the imagery.

**Action:** **Delete or rewrite.** Prefer beginning directly with the source: al-Saduq records reports identifying Fatimah with Venus and Hasan and Husayn with the Farqad stars.

---

### P-14
**Section:** The lights of one house

**Exact sentence:** “The report is not Shia property alone.”

**Defect class:** Litotes; adversarial source-as-performance narration.

**Contribution:** Indicates that versions also occur in Sunni-authored works.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the source distribution directly: “Versions also appear in al-Safuri al-Shafi‘i’s Nuzhat al-Majalis and al-Natanzi’s al-Khasa’is.”

---

### P-15
**Section:** The lights of one house

**Exact sentences:** “The five lights plus the nine stars complete a sky with exactly the figures Revelation 12:1 places around one woman, a sun she is clothed with, a moon under her feet, and twelve stars as her crown.”

**Defect class:** Decorative metaphor; obscured arithmetic.

**Contribution:** Attempts to connect the reports identifying five members of the household and nine later Imams with Revelation’s twelve stars.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the actual count explicitly. State which figures constitute the twelve Imams and how the separate sun and moon identifications relate to that count. “Complete a sky” hides a potentially confusing overlap between Ali as moon and Ali as the first of the twelve.

---

### P-16
**Section:** The lights of one house

**Exact sentences:** “The astral code above stands on its own reports. Reading Revelation 12 through that code is an inference of the argument, not a transmitted interpretation.”

**Defect class:** Vague metaphor; decorative contrast.

**Contribution:** Makes an important source-boundary distinction between transmitted Islamic interpretations and the article’s modern cross-textual inference.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the distinction precisely: the cited reports interpret Islamic passages and figures through celestial imagery, but no cited classical report applies those interpretations to Revelation 12.

---

### P-17
**Section:** The Fatimah reading and its history

**Exact sentence:** “Placed against that background, the modern Imami reading of Revelation 12 states itself.”

**Defect class:** Personification; empty transition.

**Contribution:** Introduces the modern reading.

**Action:** **Delete.** Begin with the Baydun quotation or state who proposed the reading and when.

---

### P-18
**Section:** The Fatimah reading and its history

**Exact sentences:** “The provenance of this reading must be stated exactly, because it is the weakest link in the case and a debate opponent will find it. The corpus search for the woman of Revelation 12 across the classical Imami literature, al-Kafi, the tafsirs, Bihar al-Anwar in its hundred and more volumes, returns nothing before the modern period.”

**Defect class:** Internal process leakage; debate-stage narration; undocumented search-performance claim.

**Contribution:** Supplies the crucial qualification that no classical Imami application of Revelation 12 was found.

**Action:** **Rewrite and source-review.** Preserve the historical limit, but remove the imagined opponent and narration of the research process. State the evidence-bearing result with its scope: the sources surveyed contain no premodern Imami identification of Revelation 12’s woman as Fatimah. A fidelity reviewer should verify that the stated corpus and search method justify “nothing before the modern period.”

---

### P-19
**Section:** The Fatimah reading and its history

**Exact sentence:** “Of the versions surveyed for the record above, one makes the sun Ali and the woman's travail her miscarriage of Muhsin, and one makes the woman Narjis, the Mahdi's mother, with the sun as Imam al-Hasan al-Askari.”

**Defect class:** Internal research narration; vague attribution.

**Contribution:** Records disagreement among modern Imami interpretations.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the disagreement, but identify the authors or sources of both readings. Delete “surveyed for the record above.”

---

### P-20
**Section:** The Fatimah reading and its history

**Exact sentences:** “But the modern reading is not built on air. It assembles elements the classical corpus had already fixed by transmission…”

**Defect class:** Litotes; theatrical personification; overstated abstraction.

**Contribution:** Distinguishes the modern synthesis from its older component traditions.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve that the cross-textual application is modern while some component identifications occur in earlier Islamic reports. Avoid claiming that the corpus “fixed” them unless the article has established their authority and transmission status rather than merely their attestation.

---

### P-21
**Section:** Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael

**Exact sentence:** “The Prophet descends from Ishmael through Adnan by continuous Islamic genealogy, and the Muslim tradition read this blessing with its own count in view.”

**Defect class:** Vague abstraction; personified tradition.

**Contribution:** Connects the Ishmaelite promise with Muhammad and introduces Muslim interpretations of the twelve princes.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the genealogical claim with its proper qualification and state directly that named Muslim authors interpreted the twelve princes as twelve leaders from Muhammad’s family. “With its own count in view” does not identify who made that interpretation or on what basis.

---

### P-22
**Section:** Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael

**Exact sentence:** “Majlisi went further than quotation and checked the text himself, in the seventeenth century.”

**Defect class:** Source-as-performance narration; possible overstatement.

**Contribution:** Distinguishes Majlisi’s reported consultation with People of the Book from mere repetition of an earlier quotation.

**Action:** **Rewrite and source-review.** Preserve exactly what Majlisi claims: he says he heard the Hebrew text and its translation from trustworthy People of the Book. Do not call this checking “the text himself” unless evidence shows that he independently read or collated a Hebrew Torah manuscript.

---

### P-23
**Section:** Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael

**Exact sentences:** “The honest classification of this whole line is a reading of the Torah made by Muslims, resting in its strongest form, al-Nu'mani's, on the dictation of a named Jewish scholar, not on a chain to an Imam. After al-Nu'mani and al-Rawandi it becomes a standing argument, carried by al-Hurr al-Amili through al-Bayadi and by later scholars in dozens of volumes.”

**Defect class:** Self-certification; vague source-volume performance.

**Contribution:** Correctly separates Muslim interpretation from Imam-attributed transmission and sketches its later reception.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the source classification without “honest.” Identify the later carriers needed to establish reception; “dozens of volumes” is imprecise and adds rhetorical weight rather than usable evidence.

---

### P-24
**Section:** Twelve Imams in their own reports

**Exact sentences:** “The strongest Imami hadiths fix it by transmission, and the Tablet of Fatimah is the foundation. Al-Kulayni records it in al-Kafi.”

**Defect class:** Vague evaluative abstraction; source-as-performance narration.

**Contribution:** Introduces a major Imami report naming the succession.

**Action:** **Rewrite and source-review.** Preserve that al-Kafi’s Tablet report names the succession. “Strongest” and “foundation” require hadith-critical criteria not supplied in this prose; either provide those criteria or use neutral attribution.

---

### P-25
**Section:** Twelve Imams in their own reports

**Exact sentence:** “Beside the Tablet, the count is stated in the plainest words in five independent classical works.”

**Defect class:** Source-as-performance narration; potentially imprecise independence claim.

**Contribution:** Introduces additional attestations of the twelve-Imam count.

**Action:** **Rewrite and source-review.** Name the works and state whether they preserve genuinely independent chains or reproduce a common report. “Plainest words” is editorial praise, and “independent” requires verification.

---

### P-26
**Section:** Twelve Imams in their own reports

**Exact sentences:** “The opponents' own widespread reports validate the Imami reports about the twelve Imams. And al-Kafi carries the comparison Jesus himself had already provided.”

**Defect class:** Adversarial source-as-performance narration; overstatement; personification.

**Contribution:** Reports al-Saduq’s argument from Sunni twelve-caliph traditions and introduces an Imami comparison with the twelve trustees of Jesus.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Attribute the first conclusion to al-Saduq rather than presenting validation as established. For the second, say that al-Kafi transmits a report comparing Muhammad’s twelve trustees with Jesus’s twelve trustees; the present wording incorrectly makes Jesus himself the provider of the comparison.

---

### P-27
**Section:** Twelve Imams in their own reports

**Exact sentence:** “A kunyah is an honorific byname, Abu so-and-so, and the report's point is that the twelfth one is publicly no one at all until he rises.”

**Defect class:** Irony; misleading overstatement.

**Contribution:** Explains an unfamiliar term and the report’s claim of concealed identity.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Keep the definition of *kunyah*. Preserve that the report withholds the twelfth figure’s public name and kunyah until his appearance. Delete “publicly no one at all,” which turns concealment into a theatrical and potentially inaccurate formulation.

---

### P-28
**Section:** Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon

**Exact sentence:** “The Sunni collections carry the number with chains their own scholars grade at the top of the canon.”

**Defect class:** Vague source prestige; adversarial “their own” framing.

**Contribution:** Establishes that the twelve-caliph report occurs in highly authoritative Sunni collections.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** State directly that Sahih Muslim includes the report through several chains. If later grading is relevant, name the scholars and grades rather than invoking “the top of the canon.”

---

### P-29
**Section:** Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon

**Exact sentences:** “The Sunni tradition itself struggled with the number, and its own commentary says so. The answers show the problem. A number that the canon fixes, and that history overruns, had to be dissolved by interpretation, and one answer quietly turns the prophecy into a tally of past rulers.”

**Defect class:** Personification; adversarial irony; theatrical abstraction.

**Contribution:** Argues that Sunni commentators faced difficulty identifying a limited set of twelve rulers after more than twelve caliphs had reigned.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the concrete interpretive problem and al-Qadi Iyad’s solution. State that al-Qadi reads the report as predicting at least twelve rulers rather than limiting all rulers to twelve. Delete “struggled,” “history overruns,” “dissolved,” and “quietly,” which stage the disagreement instead of analyzing it.

---

### P-30
**Section:** Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon

**Exact sentences:** “That report reads the Mahdi as an Abbasid caliph, and it is counterevidence of a kind. It shows that within the Sunni corpus the number was pressed onto whatever rulers a reader knew, which is what a fixed number without its bearers produces.”

**Defect class:** Vague qualification; sweeping generalization; derisive abstraction.

**Contribution:** Identifies an Abbasid interpretation as evidence that the number received competing historical applications.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve only what the cited report supports: this report applies the sequence to Abbasid figures and therefore demonstrates one competing Sunni identification. It cannot by itself establish that readers generally imposed the number on “whatever rulers” they knew.

---

### P-31
**Section:** The king who reigns in righteousness

**Exact sentence:** “None of this occurred in the first century. The Gospel's own record states the point against itself.”

**Defect class:** Irony; personification; adversarial source narration.

**Contribution:** States the historical premise that the cited public and political outcomes did not occur during Jesus’s first advent and introduces John 18:36.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the historical claim and introduce the quotation neutrally. John 18:36 may be relevant to the nature of Jesus’s kingdom, but the Gospel does not “state a point against itself.”

---

### P-32
**Section:** The king who reigns in righteousness

**Exact sentences:** “The standard Christian answer is that the promises await the second coming, and that answer concedes the essential point. They were not fulfilled by the first advent.”

**Defect class:** Debate-performance narration; loaded “concedes.”

**Contribution:** Identifies the relevant Christian qualification and the shared premise that complete fulfillment remains future.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the shared premise directly: Christian interpretations that place these outcomes at the second coming also hold that they were not completed during the first advent.

---

### P-33
**Section:** The king who reigns in righteousness

**Exact sentences:** “Once the Christian concedes the fulfillment is future, the dispute changes its shape. It is no longer whether the prophecies await a future just ruler. It is who that ruler is, and whether the returning Isa is himself the king or stands behind another.”

**Defect class:** Theatrical personification; unnecessary adversarial framing.

**Contribution:** Narrows the article’s disagreement with futurist Christian interpretation.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the distinction: if fulfillment is future, the remaining disagreement concerns whether Jesus personally exercises the described rule or whether another ruler does so when Jesus returns. Remove “concedes” and the dispute “changing shape.”

---

### P-34
**Section:** The king who reigns in righteousness

**Exact sentence:** “The table's claims are about public history, and any reader can check them against any chronicle of the first centuries.”

**Defect class:** Source-as-performance narration; vague evidentiary assurance.

**Contribution:** Claims that the table’s historical assertions are independently verifiable.

**Action:** **Delete or source-review.** The article should cite appropriate historical evidence for disputed claims. An assurance that “any reader” can consult “any chronicle” is not evidence and overstates uniformity among chronicles.

---

### P-35
**Section:** The ruler who fills the earth with justice

**Exact sentence:** “Against that job description the Islamic corpus sets a named candidate, from the Prophet's own house, from Fatimah's children.”

**Defect class:** Theatrical personification.

**Contribution:** Introduces Mahdi reports as the proposed Islamic match for the biblical ruler.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** State directly that the following Sunni and Shia reports identify the Mahdi as a descendant of Muhammad and Fatimah and describe him as filling the earth with justice.

---

### P-36
**Section:** The ruler who fills the earth with justice

**Exact sentences:** “The decisive distinction is the one the reports draw themselves. The returning Isa is present, and another is the imam.”

**Defect class:** Source-as-performance narration; premature evaluative emphasis.

**Contribution:** States the important distinction between the returning Jesus and the imam in the cited reports.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the distinction without calling it “decisive”: the cited reports describe Jesus returning while an imam from the Muslim community is already present. The subsequent Shia reports identify that imam as the Mahdi.

---

### P-37
**Section:** The ruler who fills the earth with justice

**Exact sentence:** “And Imam al-Hasan gives the tradition its sharpest form.”

**Defect class:** Source-as-performance narration; vague evaluation.

**Contribution:** Introduces a report emphasizing that Jesus prays behind the Qa’im and that the Qa’im bears no allegiance to a temporal ruler.

**Action:** **Delete or rewrite.** Introduce the specific claim directly. “Sharpest” supplies no historical or analytical information.

---

### P-38
**Section:** The ruler who fills the earth with justice

**Exact sentences:** “This is why the Davidic prophecies fit the Shia framework without violence. The framework already distinguishes the returning Isa, who confirms the truth, from the divinely guided ruler of the final order.”

**Defect class:** Litotes; self-certification; vague abstraction.

**Contribution:** Explains why the author believes Shia eschatology can assign distinct roles to Jesus and the Mahdi.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the role distinction directly. The cited Shia reports describe Jesus returning and praying behind the Mahdi; the article therefore proposes the Mahdi as the earthly ruler while Jesus has a distinct role. Delete “fit,” “without violence,” “confirms the truth,” and “final order” unless each is defined and sourced.

---

### P-39
**Section:** What the case establishes and what it does not

**Exact sentence:** “On textual fidelity the comparison is even in one direction.”

**Defect class:** Vague abstraction; unclear evaluative comparison.

**Contribution:** Appears intended to claim an evidentiary advantage for the Islamic reading.

**Action:** **Rewrite or delete.** If retained, identify the exact asymmetry: the cited Islamic reports explicitly identify their own sun, moon, twelve successors, and Mahdi, whereas Revelation leaves its figures unnamed. Do not call that “textual fidelity” without explaining the criterion.

---

### P-40
**Section:** What the case establishes and what it does not

**Exact sentences:** “What the case does establish survives that concession. If the promised Messiah has already come and completed his messianic work, where are the outcomes the prophets promised, the universal law, the peace among nations, the destroyed oppressor kingdoms, the gathered and secure Israel, the worldwide justice?”

## Inspection Scope

I inspected the title, front matter summary, abstract, section headings, fact-card wording, every authored paragraph surrounding the callouts, table prose, bullet summaries, and the Final Verdict. The source quotations and paired translations inside callouts were treated as protected source text and were not stylistically rewritten. Authored introductions, attributions, source assessments, and conclusions surrounding those callouts remained within scope.

The principal recurring defects are source-as-performance narration, claims of editorial honesty or methodological restraint, personified corpora and arguments, adversarial concessions, and slogan-like repetitions of “job description” versus “identity.” Necessary negations and qualifications were retained as substantive where they limit the historical or textual claim.

## Necessary Passages Retained

The following apparent repetitions are necessary rather than economy defects:

- The minority interpretation of Qur'an 91 must remain because it qualifies the claim about the dominant Imami mapping.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the narrower finding: this assignment has more identified carriers in the surveyed riwa’i corpus than the recorded alternative. Use “more widely attested in the surveyed transmitted-tafsir sources” unless reception evidence establishes school-wide dominance.

---

### R-04
**Section:** The Fatimah reading and its history

**Exact sentences:**
> “The line of argument enters Muslim literature through convert polemicists of the nineteenth century, and Imami authors adopted and developed it in the twentieth.”

**Defect class:** Unsupported historical generalization; provenance stated as fact.

**What it contributes:** It identifies the historical route by which the Revelation 12 interpretation supposedly entered Imami writing.

**Problem:** The evidence displayed establishes an early-fourteenth-century-AH carrier and later authors, but it does not independently establish that convert polemicists originated the argument or that this was its route into Muslim literature. “Enters Muslim literature through” is a historical conclusion requiring identified works, dates, and evidence of dependence.

**Action:** **Source-review.** Verify the relevant nineteenth-century convert texts, their dates, and demonstrable dependence by later Imami authors. If dependence cannot be shown, rewrite to preserve only the documented chronology: no earlier carrier was found in the searched corpus, and the earliest identified explicit Imami use is al-Ha’iri.

---

### R-05
**Section:** Twelve princes from the seed of Ishmael

**Exact sentences:**
> “The Bible promises twelve princes from Ishmael. The Islamic corpus counts twelve Imams from Ishmael's greatest descendant. The numerical link is a reasoned reading of Genesis 17:20, and its classical home in the school is the Ghayba of al-Nu'mani.”

**Defect class:** Material biblical counterevidence omitted.

**What it contributes:** It presents Genesis 17:20 as an open numerical description that can be matched to the twelve Imams.

**Problem:** Genesis later names Ishmael’s twelve sons and explicitly calls them twelve princes according to their nations (Genesis 25:13-16). That is the most immediate canonical fulfillment of Genesis 17:20. Without addressing it, the article treats a text with named biblical referents as though its number remained unassigned. A secondary typological application may still be argued, but it cannot be presented as the straightforward identification.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the existence and antiquity of the Imami ta’wil, but state that Genesis itself identifies Ishmael’s twelve princes as his twelve sons. Then distinguish direct historical referent from a proposed typological or secondary application to the Imams.

---

### R-06
**Section:** The king who reigns in righteousness

**Exact sentences:**
> “Jesus ﵇ before Pilate refuses the political kingdom.”

**Defect class:** Interpretive overstatement.

**What it contributes:** It separates Jesus’ first advent from the governmental reign described in the prophetic texts.

**Problem:** John 18:36 says that Jesus’ kingdom is not “from” this world and that his servants therefore were not fighting to prevent his arrest. It does not unambiguously renounce every future public or political reign. The article later correctly limits the argument to nonfulfillment during the first advent, but this sentence makes the stronger claim.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the narrower point: before Pilate, Jesus does not inaugurate or defend an earthly kingdom by force, and the public outcomes listed from the prophets did not occur during his first advent.

---

### R-07
**Section:** The king who reigns in righteousness / The ruler who fills the earth with justice

**Exact sentences:**
> “The standard Christian answer is that the promises await the second coming, and that answer concedes the essential point.”

> “This is why the Davidic prophecies fit the Shia framework without violence.”

> “The Gospels' Isa ﵇ refused the kingdom before Pilate, and the reports of both traditions give the earthly throne to a man from the Prophet's ﷺ house while Isa ﵇ stands behind him in prayer.”

**Defect class:** The second-coming reply remains unresolved; lineage and office are conflated.

**What it contributes:** It argues that the Christian postponement of fulfillment leaves an opening that the Mahdi reports fill more specifically.

**Problem:** The concession establishes only that the cited outcomes were not completed at the first advent. It does not transfer the Davidic office to another person. Isaiah 11 and Jeremiah 23 identify the ruler through Jesse and David, a qualification Jesus satisfies within Christian interpretation and the Mahdi does not satisfy on the genealogy presented here. Similar functions such as justice, rule, and worldwide peace do not erase that lineage condition. Nor does prayer behind another person necessarily assign all Davidic royal functions to that imam. The Sunni report quoted here says only that Jesus descends while “your imam is from among you”; it neither names the imam as the Mahdi nor explicitly gives him the throne described by Isaiah, Jeremiah, Psalms, and Daniel.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the valid argument that first-advent fulfillment is incomplete and that Islamic reports distinguish the returning Jesus from an end-time imam. Concede that the Christian second-coming reading remains textually viable because of the Davidic lineage, and present the Mahdi identification as a cross-traditional functional comparison rather than as the result forced by the biblical descriptions.

---

### R-08
**Section:** What the case establishes and what it does not

**Exact sentences:**
> “The question left standing is the one the Gospels posed, whether the returning one is himself the reigning king or stands behind another. The reports of both traditions describe that other as a man from the Prophet's ﷺ house, from the children of Fatimah כֿ, whose reign is earthly, public, and just.”

**Defect class:** False source attribution; independent reports merged into a shared conclusion.

**What it contributes:** It frames the final dispute as one already posed by the Gospels and answered jointly by Sunni and Shia reports.

**Problem:** The Gospels do not pose this either-or question. It is the article’s comparative question. The Sunni materials quoted separately attest a Mahdi from Fatimah’s descendants and an unnamed imam present when Jesus descends; the explicitly fused identification and prayer-behind-Mahdi reports shown are Imami. Presenting the combined conclusion as what “both traditions describe” suppresses that inferential join.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the comparative question but attribute it to the article. Distinguish the evidence: Sunni reports provide the Mahdi traditions and an unnamed imam at Jesus’ descent; the quoted Imami reports explicitly identify that imam as the Mahdi and place Jesus behind him in prayer.

---

### R-09
**Section:** What the case establishes and what it does not / Final Verdict

**Exact sentences:**
> “On textual fidelity the comparison is even in one direction. The Islamic corpus fixes each element by transmission, the sun as the Prophet ﷺ and the moon as Ali ﵇ in the exegesis of Qur'an 91, the twelve stars as the Imams in the Salman report, the twelve count in both canons, and the justice-filling ruler from Fatimah's ﵍ line.”

> “The Qur'an swears by the sun and the moon, and the Imams named them the Prophet ﷺ and Ali ﵇.”

**Defect class:** Attributed reports silently upgraded; earlier numerical defect repeated.

**What it contributes:** It gives the final case an evidentiary hierarchy: Islamic identities are supposedly fixed, while only their biblical application remains inferential.

**Problem:** The article’s exhibits are attributed reports whose historical reliability is not established merely by their appearance in several collections. “The Imams named them” converts transmitted attributions into an unqualified historical act. “Fixes each element by transmission” is ambiguous and then incorrectly includes “the twelve stars as the Imams,” which the Salman report does not state in Revelation’s exact configuration. The distinction between what the sources report, what later authors infer, and what historically occurred is therefore lost at the conclusion.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the claim that the surveyed Islamic reports assign these identities within the tradition. Use formulations such as “reports attributed to the Imams identify…” and “the Salman report constructs a related sequence of celestial guides.” Do not claim that it supplies Revelation’s twelve-star configuration unless R-01 is resolved.

---

### R-10
**Section:** Twelve caliphs in the Sunni canon

**Exact sentences:**
> “The answers show the problem. A number that the canon fixes, and that history overruns, had to be dissolved by interpretation, and one answer quietly turns the prophecy into a tally of past rulers.”

**Defect class:** Authorial characterization presented as historical necessity; inadequate treatment of an opposing interpretation.

**What it contributes:** It argues that Sunni attempts to identify the twelve are ad hoc and therefore strengthen the Imami identification.

**Problem:** Al-Qadi’s position does not “dissolve” the number; it interprets the report as asserting the occurrence of twelve qualified rulers without asserting that only twelve rulers would ever exist. The article may find that reading weak, but “had to be” imputes motive and necessity rather than demonstrating a contradiction. “History overruns” also assumes exclusivity that the cited wording does not expressly contain.

**Action:** **Rewrite.** Preserve the criticism that this interpretation reduces the number’s identifying force and permits many possible selections. State the logical objection directly without presenting the commentator’s proposed resolution as an evasion established by history.
